expertise:
LLM application architecture — Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline: (1) Ingestion — document parsing (PDF → unstructured.io/PyMuPDF, HTML → trafilatura/beautifulsoup, code → tree-sitter AST, multimodal → CLIP embeddings for images), chunking strategy (fixed-size with overlap — 512 tokens + 128 overlap for general, sentence-based for QA, recursive character split with separators: 

 → 
 → → no split — preserves semantic boundaries, semantic chunking via embedding similarity threshold), (2) Embedding — model selection (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small — 1536d $0.02/1M tokens, Cohere Embed v3 — 1024d input_type classification, voyage-2 — 1024d, all with MTEB benchmark comparison per task type), vector DB (Pinecone — fully managed, serverless indexes, metadata filtering, $0.33/GB/month, Weaviate — open-source, hybrid search BM25+vector, Qdrant — Rust-based, quantization: binary/product/scalar, Milvus — distributed, GPU-accelerated index builds, Zilliz Cloud — managed Milvus, pgvector — PostgreSQL extension, HNSW/IVFFlat indexes, pgvector 0.6+ supports HNSW, simplest for existing PG shops), (3) Retrieval — hybrid search (sparse BM25 for keyword precision + dense vector for semantic recall — reciprocal rank fusion to combine scores: RRF(d) = Σ 1/(k+rank_i(d)), k=60 typical), reranking (cross-encoder Cohere Rerank/ BGE-reranker-v2/ ColBERT — expensive but high quality, applied to top-K candidate chunks from retrieval), query transformations (HyDE — generate hypothetical answer → embed answer → retrieve similar, multi-query — generate multiple search queries from user question → deduplicate results, step-back — generate broader question → retrieve general context → combine with specific), (4) Generation — prompt assembly (system prompt + retrieved context chunks with source citations + conversation history + user query, context window management — reserve 60-70% for context, 30-40% for generation, truncate context chunks via relevance score cutoff or summarization of overflow), citation (inline citation markers [1] [2] with references section, source grounding — require answer to cite specific context chunk or flag as 'insufficient information').

Evaluation and quality — automated metrics: RAGAS framework (faithfulness — % claims in answer with citation from context, answer relevancy — semantic similarity between answer and question, context precision — signal-to-noise of retrieved chunks, context recall — coverage of ground truth answer in retrieved context), BLEU/ROUGE (limited for generative QA — penalizes valid rephrasing), LLM-as-judge (GPT-4 evaluation on 1-5 scale for correctness/helpfulness/harmlessness, correlation with human eval: Pearson r=0.7-0.85 for most benchmarks), human evaluation (inter-rater reliability with Krippendorff's alpha, evaluation rubric with anchored examples per score level, blind A/B testing for production changes). Grounding and hallucination reduction: chain-of-verification (generate answer → generate verification questions → answer questions independently → check consistency → revise if inconsistent), retrieval-augmented confidence scores (if answer claims supported by high-relevance chunks → high confidence, if answer uses low-relevance chunks or no chunks → low confidence), factuality evaluation (attribution to source, contradiction detection within answer, factual consistency with context — specialized NLI model trained for this task).

Production ML systems — feature store (Tecton/Feast/Hopsworks — offline features from batch data warehouse, online features from real-time stream for low-latency serving, feature freshness monitoring, point-in-time correct training data generation to prevent data leakage), model serving (real-time — <100ms latency: Triton Inference Server/ Ray Serve/ BentoML with GPU, batch — hourly/daily: Spark/Databricks jobs with model registry, streaming — Kafka → Flink/Beam → model → output topic), MLOps pipeline (data validation → feature engineering → training → evaluation → registry → deployment → monitoring — each step versioned and reproducible, experiment tracking with MLflow/Weights & Biases/Neptune, model registry with stage transitions: Staging → Production → Archived, deployment strategies: canary (10% traffic → 50% → 100%), shadow (copy traffic to new model, compare predictions, no user impact), A/B (random split, measure business metrics). Monitoring: data drift (PSI — Population Stability Index, KS statistic for feature distributions, drift detection with evidentlyai/nannyml/whylogs — trigger retraining when drift exceeds threshold), model performance (regression metrics over time, prediction distribution shift — are we predicting more high-risk than before? bias metrics by subgroup — are protected groups getting systematically different outcomes?), pipeline health (data freshness, schema changes, missing values spike, training job duration trend).
